_comment: OTA-1086 — stage business for a conversation. One short beat of what somebody DOES while they answer you. See app/engine/flourish.ts for why these are authored rather than generated, and why the model can only ever replace one of these lines rather than delay it. {npc} is substituted with the person's name.

forge: {npc} keeps working while they talk — a rag over a joint, a thumb testing an edge that did not need testing.
Something in the back of {npc}'s shop ticks over and settles, and they do not look up at it.
{npc} sets a cooling billet down on the stone between you like a piece of punctuation.
There is a burn on the back of {npc}'s hand old enough to have stopped being a story.
{npc} talks at the anvil rather than at you, which is habit more than rudeness.
arms: {npc} turns a piece over twice while they speak and puts it back facing the other way.
Nothing on {npc}'s rack is dusty, and you notice that they notice you noticing.
{npc} keeps one hand loose on the counter, near enough to the good stock to mean it.
Half of what {npc} says is aimed at you and half at the state of your gear.
{npc} glances at what you are carrying and their mouth does something small.
counter: {npc} counts something under the counter without looking down, and does not lose the count.
The tally slate behind {npc} has three names chalked on it and you cannot read them upside down.
{npc} shifts a crate six inches to the left for no reason either of you could name.
{npc} answers you and finishes a sum at the same time, and neither one suffers for it.
A tin of chits goes into {npc}'s apron pocket in the middle of the sentence.
curio: {npc} sets down whatever they were holding, very gently, before they answer.
Something in {npc}'s case catches the lamp, and they turn it away from the light.
{npc}'s fingers keep finding the edge of the tray and letting go of it again.
Nothing on {npc}'s table is labelled, and you get the sense they prefer it that way.
books: {npc} keeps a finger in a page the whole time, on the chance that you turn out to be brief.
{npc} stops to get the wording right, which takes longer than the thought did.
There is ink on {npc}'s knuckle, fresh enough to still be wet at the edge.
{npc} answers you the way people answer a question they have already written down somewhere.
field: {npc} looks past you at the weather while they talk, out of a habit the road gave them.
{npc} checks a strap hanging on the wall without appearing to decide to.
{npc} tests a coil of rope against their knee and keeps talking over the creak of it.
{npc} keeps their voice low enough that it does not carry past the doorway.
quarters: {npc} says it as though it has already been written down somewhere and signed.
{npc} does not sit, and does not offer you anywhere to.
Something is being counted behind {npc}, and neither of you acknowledges it.
{npc} waits a beat before each answer, the way people do when the answer is policy.
road: {npc} keeps facing the way they were going, and talks to you sideways.
{npc} shifts the pack higher on their shoulder and does not put it down.
{npc} looks at the road behind you before they answer anything at all.
Whatever {npc} is chewing goes over to the other cheek.
escort: {npc} counts their people while they talk, and the count comes out right.
{npc} answers you without breaking stride, because stopping costs more than it looks.
{npc} keeps their eyes up on the ridgeline through most of it.
guardian: {npc} does not move at all while they speak, and the stillness is the loudest part of it.
The air near {npc} does what air does near Aether, and neither of you mentions it.
{npc} answers as though the answer had been waiting somewhere a long time for the question.

stranger: {npc} keeps the counter between you the whole time, which is only sense.
{npc} gives you the short version, and you can hear that it is the short version.
met: {npc} places you, roughly, and adjusts what they were about to say.
There is half a nod in it — you are a face now, if not much more than one.
known: {npc} lets the sentence run longer than they would for a stranger.
{npc} has stopped checking where your hands are.
familiar: {npc} uses your name in the middle of it without making anything of it.
{npc} talks to you while doing something else, which is its own kind of trust.
trusted: {npc} drops their voice, though there is nobody in here but the two of you.
{npc} tells you the thing and then waits, to see what you do with it.
wronged: {npc} does not stop watching your hands, and does not pretend otherwise.
{npc} keeps three feet and a hard look between you the whole time.

fallback: {npc} takes a moment with it before answering.
{npc} looks at you a beat longer than the question needed.
